name: CAMUS
aliases: Complementary and Alternative Medicine for Urological Symptoms
question: Does escalating an ethanolic saw palmetto fruit extract to three times the usual dose improve male lower urinary tract symptoms more than placebo?

design.population: Men aged at least 45 years with AUASI 8–24 at two screening visits and peak urinary flow at least 4 mL/s.
design.description: Multicenter, double-blind, placebo-controlled randomized superiority trial
design.locator: Full text, Participants and Results/Figure 1; ClinicalTrials.gov NCT00603304, Participant Flow

verdictNote: The prespecified one-sided superiority test was not met at 72 weeks.
takeaway: In CAMUS, escalating an ethanolic saw palmetto extract from 320 to 960 mg daily did not improve 72-week AUASI scores more than matching placebo; the mean between-group change favored placebo by 0.79 points (one-sided P = 0.91).

reports.label: Primary symptom report
reports.citation: Barry MJ, Meleth S, Lee JY, et al. "Effect of increasing doses of saw palmetto extract on lower urinary tract symptoms: a randomized trial." *JAMA.* 2011;306(12):1344–1351. doi:10.1001/jama.2011.1364
reports.followUpLocator: Full text, Outcomes and Results; Table 2

results.measure: Mean change from baseline to week 72; between-group mean difference, saw palmetto minus placebo
results.note: Difference favored placebo; prespecified one-sided alpha 0.05. Upper bound of the one-sided 95% CI most favorable to saw palmetto was 1.77 points.
results.locator: Full text, Results and Table 2; PubMed abstract, Results

results.measure: At least 3-point AUASI decrease at week 72
results.note: One-sided Fisher exact test; response numerators not reported in the article text.

results.measure: Mean change from baseline to week 72
results.note: One-sided comparison; no prespecified secondary multiplicity adjustment.

delivery.label: Dose escalation and formulation
delivery.value: Proprietary lipidic ethanolic Serenoa repens extract (PROSTA-URGENIN UNO): 320, 640, then 960 mg daily, each for 24 weeks; placebo capsules escalated identically.

delivery.label: Treatment completion
delivery.value: 306 participants completed 72 weeks on treatment (151 saw palmetto, 155 placebo); all reached triple dose.

delivery.label: Visit attendance and pill count
delivery.value: 97.0% of scheduled visits were attended, excluding visits after dropouts; median pill count was 98.2% across attended visits.

reports.label: Safety analysis
reports.citation: Avins AL, Lee JY, Meyers CM, et al. "Safety and toxicity of saw palmetto in the CAMUS trial." *J Urol.* 2013;189(4):1415–1420. doi:10.1016/j.juro.2012.10.002

harms.locator: Full text, Results, Serious Adverse Events
harms.note: Modified intention-to-treat safety population; 18 versus 17 serious adverse events, respectively; two-sided P = 1.00.

harms.locator: Full text, Results, Non-Serious Adverse Events

results.note: Secondary analysis; observed SDs were 0.83 and 1.08 ng/mL, respectively.

relations.note: After STEP found no symptom benefit at 320 mg daily, CAMUS tested escalating doses through 960 mg daily.
